coverage.notes: CCIP Direct Staking documentation cross-check on 2026-09-17: all 31 network/address pairs listed at https://docs.lido.fi/deployed-contracts/#ccip-direct-staking are represented (7 Ethereum, 6 Arbitrum, 6 Optimism, 6 Base, 6 Linea). Network identity follows each linked explorer domain. The four existing PriceOracle entries are documented separately under #price-feeds and are outside this 31-entry count. This check establishes ledger coverage of the cited documentation; source revisions, deployed bytecode, and current proxy slots were not reverified.

Soneium, Unichain, Lisk, and Swellchain Emergency Brakes Safes appear on docs.lido.fi/deployed-contracts/#emergency-brakes-multisigs but have no dedicated subsection on docs.lido.fi/multisigs/emergency-brakes (Swellchain shares address 0xC2b778… with BSC; the BSC subsection is not used as a Swellchain publicRef).

The 15 Safe multisig entries record contractName 'Safe' and deploymentKind 'standalone'; neither has been established from the bytecode at those addresses. A Safe deployed through SafeProxyFactory holds GnosisSafeProxy (v1.3.0) or SafeProxy (v1.4.x) bytecode and delegates to the Safe singleton at a different address, which would make these entries proxies. Correcting them requires reading the deployed bytecode and the singleton address per network.

Chainlink CCIP Direct Staking deployments were added on 2026-08-14 from docs.lido.fi/deployed-contracts/ anchors #ethereum-common-ccip-ds, #ethereum-part-{arbitrum,optimism,base,linea}, #{arbitrum,optimism,base,linea}-part and #price-feeds: 35 addresses across eip155:1, 10, 8453, 42161 and 59144. Contract names come from each chain's verified artifact and proxy links from EIP-1967 slot reads, not from the documentation's grouping. Several of these addresses are reused across networks for different contracts, so they are only identifiable as (networkId, address) pairs; an address-only comparison against this ledger will produce false matches.

Every CCIP Direct Staking deployment records a source.commit confirmed by a Diffyscan source match on 2026-08-14, across 15 cohorts. The revisions were found by comparing git blob hashes of each explorer-verified file against repository trees, not taken from a branch head: Aphyla/chainlink-csr is a third-party fork that lidofinance/l2-direct-staking pins by branch (main) rather than by revision, so its head is not evidence of what was deployed. Ethereum needs two chainlink-csr cohorts because LineaAdapterL1toL2 verifies only at 62108f7b6cc664e36dbc8100c4b48974d59f572e while the other four L1 contracts verify at 1f33d88d56a01d24591d7e1ca4d7017a1f59e8ed. PausableImmutableOraclePool is recorded against chainlink-csr because that repository owns the file, but its verified bundle was compiled from the l2-direct-staking checkout and carries lib/chainlink-csr/ paths; the chainlink-csr profile resolves them with a self-referential dependency pinned to the cohort commit.

source.repositoryUrl is not written under one rule across the ledger. Entries added on 2026-08-14 name the repository whose git tree contains the compiled file, so OpenZeppelin artifacts cite OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts. Most earlier entries name the deployment project instead; for example eip155:59144:0xB5beDd42000b71FddE22D3eE8a79Bd49A568fC8F and eip155:59144:0xF951d7592e03eDB0Bab3D533935e678Ce64Eb927 cite lidofinance/linea-contracts-fix at 0949c4096664e613f73ed3ce51c32f97fc56cdef, whose tree contains neither TransparentUpgradeableProxy.sol nor ProxyAdmin.sol (they are build-time node_modules paths). Which rule an entry follows is not marked.

research.lido.fi/t/emergency-brakes-multi-sig-upgrade/2608 was cited by the Optimism and Arbitrum Emergency Brakes entries but names neither address. All 3 posts of the topic were read through the Discourse API on 2026-08-24: it is a 2/4 to 3/5 proposal for the Ethereum Easy Track multisig, naming six signer EOAs and a snapshot proposal id, and on the L2 Safes it is forward-looking only ("Set up multi-sigs of the same composition to manage pause levers on other networks ... starting with Optimism and Arbitrum in the nearest future"). Those two citations were removed on 2026-08-26; both entries keep three refs that do name their address in visible text. eip155:1:0x73b047fe6337183A454c5217241D780a932777bD still cites the topic, which names that address only inside a link target (gnosis-safe.io/app/eth:0x73b047fe.../settings/owners), so an automated check finds it while a reader sees only the words "this 2/4 multi-sig".

Two Linea entries pin a revision that is a near neighbour of the deployed source but not the revision the explorer verified, and no public revision that matches was found on 2026-08-26. eip155:59144:0x74Be82F00CC867614803ffd7f36A2a4aF0405670 (LineaBridgeExecutor) is byte-identical to lidofinance/governance-crosschain-bridges@7d4fd35e in 5 of 6 files; contracts/bridges/LineaBridgeExecutor.sol differs in one NatSpec line (@author Aave in the repository, @author Linea in the verified bundle, whose blob is 4cc3fe27c5d5e3f53adafecc5ab6a304399889cd against 61919ee2cb1639ce64a3013ceaa28e7127273310 at the pin). That file exists on no branch head of the repository, and no commit along either parent chain of the pinned merge serves the verified blob. eip155:59144:0xc0583e2F5930EDE5Fab9D57bAC4169878730B010 (CustomBridgedToken) is byte-identical to lidofinance/linea-contracts@3cf85529 in 15 of 17 files; contracts/tokenBridge/BridgedToken.sol (verified blob 63ab1365fdd3706ea65566282b9506030a1d37c4) and contracts/tokenBridge/CustomBridgedToken.sol (verified blob e56e3edd8df86c9c32aadf57a7492e3dd1992d79) differ in NatSpec only. Neither blob is served by lidofinance/linea-contracts or by Consensys/linea-contracts, which holds the same single commit; Consensys/linea-monorepo serves the BridgedToken blob but not the CustomBridgedToken one, so no tree found so far serves the whole verified bundle. Comments do not reach bytecode, so the recorded revision remains the closest established one; re-pinning is blocked until a tree that serves those files is found.

eip155:1:0x723AEAD29acee7E9281C32D11eA4ed0070c41B13 and eip155:56:0x723AEAD29acee7E9281C32D11eA4ed0070c41B13 (ERC1967Proxy) cannot be source-verified against any repository tree. Their explorer-verified source is one hardhat-flattened file presented as ERC1967Proxy.sol ("Sources flattened with hardhat v2.22.6", ~25.8 kB, checked on 2026-08-26), not the per-file bundle a source comparison needs. The pinned wormhole-foundation/example-wormhole-axelar-wsteth@eae15a0d resolves, but serves no root-level ERC1967Proxy.sol, so every sweep answers 404 on that path and aborts the cohort at that address. The 404 is a fact about the flattened bundle rather than about the pin, and no other commit would resolve it. Until the ledger can record 'verified source is flattened' per deployment, eip155:1:0x87fc4B27385Bb4E69A40027931229d74EF4d1943 and eip155:56:0xA1eBb6A4b856dF8bf6c3aCa88a9115a9ab3b2E02 are left unrequested behind the abort, and their pins stay neither confirmed nor impeached.
